title: TRM at nano scale: the outer refinement loop is the whole story, the inner latent recursion is not
hypothesis: At ~0.1M params on 4x4 Sudoku, TRM-style recursion (arXiv:2510.04871) buys accuracy mainly through the OUTER refinement loop (repeatedly re-encoding a full candidate solution) rather than through INNER latent recursion at matched core-block applications; and per the TRM critique (arXiv:2512.11847) most of the achievable full-puzzle solve rate is already present at recursion depth 1.
question: When you split TRM recursion into its two halves and hold parameters and core-block applications exactly equal, which half buys generalization - and does solve rate saturate at recursion depth 1?
method: One 2-layer MLP core (LN -> 256x192 -> GELU -> 192x256) on a flat 256-d state (16 cells x 16-d), applied exactly T times in three arms that differ ONLY in the information path between steps: (a) outer_deepsup - state passes through the 16x4 answer distribution, re-embedded, CE loss at every step; (a') outer_finalsup - same loop, CE at the final step only (deep-supervision control); (b) inner_latent - state is the full-width 256-d latent z (z <- z + core(x+z)), decoded once at the end. T=1 is the single-pass baseline where all arms collapse to one core application. Identical param count (116,624) everywhere; full backprop through the loop (no TRM 1-step gradient approximation). Depths T in {1,2,4,8}, 3 seeds, 24 runs. 1200 steps, batch 128, AdamW lr 3e-3 (40-step warmup + cosine), wd 0.01, grad-clip 1.0; every run reaches 1.000 solve rate on the training puzzles, so this compares generalization at converged train fit.
architecture: TRM-style weight-tied 2-layer MLP recursion, 116,624 params, 16-cell flat state, T in {1,2,4,8} core applications

dataset.name: synthetic 4x4 Sudoku; all 288 valid grids enumerated, split by SOLUTION GRID into 202 train / 86 held-out; puzzles are 4-8-given maskings rejection-sampled for a unique solution (2000 train, 800 held-out-grid test, 800 seen-grid unseen-mask test; mean 9.15 blanks)
dataset.source: generated in run.py (seeded backtracking enumeration + uniqueness-checked rejection sampling)

task: 4x4 Sudoku completion (constraint satisfaction); metrics on blank cells only

metrics.headline: at matched compute the outer answer-space refinement loop scales (0.220 -> 0.513 solve rate, T=1 -> 8) while inner latent recursion is flat (0.218 -> 0.245); +0.268 solve rate for outer over inner at T=8; deep supervision is NOT the cause (final-step-only supervision is better, 0.550); the critique's '94% at recursion step 1' holds for latent recursion (89%) and fails for the refinement loop (40-43%)

result_summary: Hypothesis confirmed on the mechanism, refuted on the saturation claim - and the two results are the same finding seen from two sides. Splitting TRM recursion into mutually exclusive information paths through one identical 116k-param core at exactly matched core-block applications: the OUTER refinement loop (state passes through the 16x4 answer distribution) climbs 0.220 -> 0.339 -> 0.448 -> 0.513 held-out-grid solve rate at T=1/2/4/8, while INNER latent recursion (full-width 256-d z, decoded once) is essentially flat at 0.218 -> 0.245 over the same 8x compute, a +0.268 gap at T=8 with per-cell seed std <= 0.030. Latent depth is not merely useless: its held-out cell accuracy DECREASES with depth (0.760 -> 0.737) while its seen-grid solve rate rises 0.533 -> 0.722, i.e. extra latent recursion buys memorization capacity rather than constraint propagation. TRM-style deep supervision is not the cause of the outer loop's win - supervising only the final step is better (0.550 vs 0.513 at T=8, and 0.409 vs 0.339 at T=2). The TRM critique's '94% of performance at recursion step 1' therefore splits by which recursion is ablated: fraction of best-depth solve rate already present at T=1 is 0.89 for inner latent (claim roughly holds) but only 0.40-0.43 for the outer refinement loop (claim refuted). Caveats: one task, a 16-cell CSP with only 288 total solutions, 1200 steps, and the outer curve is still rising at T=8 so its saturation point was not found.

novelty_check.conclusion: TRM (2510.04871, 7M params, 9x9 Sudoku-Extreme/ARC/Maze) ablates the recursion COUNTS n and T inside its full architecture, and the ARC-AGI-1 critique (2512.11847) reports most performance at recursion step 1; allthingssecurity/trm_sudoku is a reimplementation, not an ablation. No prior work found that isolates the two recursion mechanisms as MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE information paths through one identical core at exactly matched core-block applications, adds a deep-supervision control, or evaluates on held-out SOLUTION GRIDS rather than held-out puzzles. arXiv/OpenAlex APIs 403'd from this environment; used web search.
